subject: SDLC evidence: keystore rotation, CI controls and secrets provenance
messages:
From: Eleanor Reed <eleanor.reed@secureassessor.com>
To: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 8 Nov 2024 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: SDLC evidence request: keystore rotation + CI controls

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks for taking this on. Clearmeta is running a SIG/SOC2 intake for our upcoming assessment window and we need a concise package focused on your Secure SDLC controls. At minimum we need: a short index of artifacts, CI/CD role mappings, the keystore/rotation log for the last 12 months, and a short narrative (1-2 paragraphs) describing your emergency change approval flow.

Target delivery for the first pass is COB Friday 2024-11-15. If anything looks like it will take longer, flag it now. Please attach artifacts as small CSV/PDF stubs; we do not need full system extracts.

Questions we commonly ask:
- Where are secrets stored (KMS/HSM/provider)?
- Who has rights to rotate keys and how is that approval captured?
- Which CI jobs run as ephemeral principals vs. service accounts?

If you can provide a Drive link to artifacts + a short timeline mapping requests to filenames, that will speed review.

Regards,
Eleanor Reed
Senior Assessor, SecureAssessor

---
(Attachment requests: please reference filenames in your reply)

From: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Eleanor Reed <eleanor.reed@secureassessor.com>
Cc: jordan.blake@redwood.com, irene.choi@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 8 Nov 2024 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SDLC evidence request: keystore rotation + CI controls

Hi Eleanor — thanks for the clear list. We're on it. Plan below (assignments and artifacts):

1) sdlc-evidence-index.pdf (this thread) — high-level index and one-paragraph narrative for emergency change approval. (I will draft.)
2) ci-pipeline-roles.csv — Jordan to export role-to-job mappings and note ephemeral vs service accounts. (Jordan action)
3) keystore-rotation-log-2024Q3.csv — Irene to pull rotation timestamps, actor, and approval reference (KMS audit ids). (Irene action)
4) emergency-change-runbook.pdf — short runbook & approval trace for emergency patching. (I will attach final)

Jordan / Irene — target to me: EOD Tuesday 2024-11-12 so I can assemble and upload to Drive by 2024-11-13 for initial review. If either of you anticipate blocking issues (PII redactions, long export times), call it out in-line.

A couple quick answers to your bullet questions:
- Secrets storage: primary KMS is AWS KMS (multi-account CMKs), short-lived provisioning tokens issued by our vaulting layer (HashiCorp Vault) for runner jobs.
- Rotation approvals: rotation is performed by an automated orchestration on a scheduled cadence; manual rotations require ticketed approval in Jira (see runbook attachment).

I'll attach the index and runbook when assembled.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Customer Security Programs
Redwood Inference

(Attachment placeholders: sdlc-evidence-index.pdf; emergency-change-runbook.pdf)

From: jordan.blake@redwood.com <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com
Cc: irene.choi@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 9 Nov 2024 14:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SDLC evidence request: keystore rotation + CI controls

Vanessa — quick export notes and attached CSV stub. Attached: ci-pipeline-roles.csv (columns: job_name, repo, agent_type, principal_type, principal_id, last_changed). Highlights:
- Ephemeral principals: runner jobs that call external deploy APIs receive short-lived Vault tokens (TTL 5m). These are created by our CI controller and tied to the PR/merge build id.
- Service accounts: long-lived service accounts are limited to infra pipelines (deploy orchestration) and require 2-person approval to change binding.

I also pulled the keystore rotation entries for Q3 and Q4 into keystore-rotation-log-2024Q3.csv stub — columns include: key_id, rotated_at, initiated_by, approval_ticket, kms_audit_id. Note: the KMS audit ids map to CloudTrail events; we can provide redacted event ids if the assessor needs them.

Drive link (internal): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2B3C-sdlc-evidence (will share with Eleanor after Vanessa assembles).

Jordan Blake
Platform Security Engineer

(Attachments: ci-pipeline-roles.csv; keystore-rotation-log-2024Q3.csv)

From: Eleanor Reed <eleanor.reed@secureassessor.com>
To: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com
Cc: jordan.blake@redwood.com, irene.choi@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 10 Nov 2024 11:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SDLC evidence request: keystore rotation + CI controls

Thanks Jordan — that helps. A couple follow-ups before we close the intake:
- Can you provide an example approval ticket number for a manual rotation (redacted OK) and the related Jira link? We want to validate that approvals are ticketed and signed off by at least one approver.
- For emergency changes, we need the approval trail showing who authorized a change and who performed the operation (timestamped). If you have a recent emergency patch (last 9 months) with a short timeline, a redacted excerpt is ideal.

If you can add the runbook and a redacted approval ticket reference into the Drive folder, we can mark this intake as "package complete" for initial SIG review.

Best,
Eleanor

---
(Prefer minimal redaction; ticket numbers like RD-12345 are fine to show format)

From: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Eleanor Reed <eleanor.reed@secureassessor.com>
Cc: jordan.blake@redwood.com, irene.choi@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 10 Nov 2024 16:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SDLC evidence request: keystore rotation + CI controls

Eleanor — attached and uploaded. Summary of what I added to the Drive folder: 
1) sdlc-evidence-index.pdf — index + 2-paragraph narrative describing our emergency change approval flow (Jira ticketing, PagerDuty escalation, post-fix retrospective).
2) emergency-change-runbook.pdf — short runbook with roles, required approvals, and rollback checklist.
3) keystore-rotation-log-2024Q3.csv — redacted rotation entries; example manual ticket: RD-21437 (redacted link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/RD-21437).
4) ci-pipeline-roles.csv — role mapping and notes on ephemeral tokens.

Notes: manual rotations are rare (<5/year) and originate from a Jira ticket that includes an authorization field (Approver: SecOps Manager). Our KMS audit ids map back to CloudTrail; we redacted raw event payloads but preserved kms_audit_id values.

Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2B3C-sdlc-evidence (shared with eleanor.reed@secureassessor.com).

If you need any of the CloudTrail extracts or a short video walkthrough of the runbook, let me know and we can schedule a 30-minute session next week.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Customer Security Programs
Redwood Inference

(Attachments: sdlc-evidence-index.pdf; emergency-change-runbook.pdf; keystore-rotation-log-2024Q3.csv; ci-pipeline-roles.csv)
